newsitem.title: UK: Wood Mac downgrades UK 97 oil output, still record.
newsitem.headline: Wood Mac downgrades UK 97 oil output, still record.

text.p: Forecasts for oil output from the UK North Sea in 1997 have been revised down but production should still reach record levels, leading industry consultants Wood Mackenzie said on Monday.
Wood Mackenzie expects output to increase by 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 1996 to 2.65 million bpd.
This would represent a new peak in UK oil output, breaking a record of 2.62 million bpd set in 1985.
But the new forecast is 130,000 bpd lower than Wood Mackenzie's initial forecast of 2.78 million bpd made last December.
Production during the first half of the year failed to live up to expectations, reaching only 2.50 million bpd, some 210,000 bpd, or 8 percent down on the original forecast.
Wood Mackenzie attributed the shortfall partly to the delayed start up of four North Sea fields: Captain, Durward/Dauntless, MacCulloch and Foinaven.

"All four developments will utilise Floating Production Storage and Offloading (FPSO) systems and have been denied an earlier startup dates because of problems caused by engineering difficulties and aggressive scheduling," the consultants said in a statement.
The four projects together account for around 111,000 bpd of deferred production from the first half of 1997.
Longer-than-expected field maintenance has also eaten into production levels.
Repair work at the Brent and Bruce fields cut output for longer than was originally estimated and operational problems at the Magnus, Nelson and Scott fields also contributed, Wood Mackenzie said.
During the second half of this year, 13 new fields in the UK sector of the North Sea are scheduled to come onstream.
These include three of the four developments using floating production technology which were delayed from earlier in the year.
In addition, five subsea developments and two fixed platform developments are also scheduled for startup.
The combined output from these new projects should add an average of 183,000 bpd to North Sea oil production through the second half of the year, Wood Mackenzie said.
